name: Takayasu Arteritis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: 2022 ACR/EULAR Classification Criteria for Takayasu Arteritis

criteria.description: Blood pressure asymmetry (>10 mmHg systolic between arms)
Number of affected vascular territories on imaging
Paired vascular involvement (bilateral subclavian, bilateral renal, bilateral carotid)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Established diagnosis of large-vessel vasculitis, age <= 60, plus total weighted score >= 5
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Angiographic classification: Type I (aortic arch branches), Type IIa (ascending aorta and arch), Type IIb (ascending aorta, arch, and thoracic descending aorta), Type III (thoracic descending aorta, abdominal aorta, renal arteries), Type IV (abdominal aorta and/or renal arteries), Type V (combined features).

pathognomonic.symptomName: Pulselessness or diminished pulses in upper extremities
pathognomonic.notes: Pulseless disease; asymmetric arm blood pressures

common.notes: From renal artery stenosis; may be undetectable in arm with subclavian stenosis

laboratory: Elevated ESR and CRP (may be normal in chronic/burnt-out phase)
Pentraxin-3 may be elevated in active disease
imaging: CTA: concentric arterial wall thickening with stenosis or occlusion of aorta and branches
MRA: vessel wall edema and enhancement (active inflammation), stenosis, occlusion
PET-CT: FDG uptake in aortic wall and major branches (active disease)
Conventional angiography: stenoses, occlusions, aneurysms in aorta and branches
Doppler ultrasound: intima-media thickening (Macaroni sign) in carotid/subclavian arteries
genetic: HLA-B*52:01 strong association (especially in Japanese/Korean populations)
other: Arterial biopsy (rarely performed): granulomatous panarteritis with giant cells, intimal hyperplasia, adventitial fibrosis

redFlags: Undetectable blood pressure in one or both arms
Syncope or neurological deficits suggesting cerebrovascular compromise
Chest or back pain suggesting aortic dissection or aneurysm expansion
references: Goel R, et al. 2022 American College of Rheumatology/EULAR Classification Criteria for Takayasu Arteritis. Arthritis Rheumatol. 2022;74(12):1872-1880.
Hellmich B, et al. 2018 Update of the EULAR recommendations for the management of large vessel vasculitis. Ann Rheum Dis. 2020;79(1):19-30.
Keser G, et al. Large vessel involvement in Behcet's disease and Takayasu arteritis. Curr Opin Rheumatol. 2019;31(1):25-31.
